summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, GERD, and anxiety was admitted for two days of constant epigastric discomfort described as similar to her pre-bypass symptoms. Initial concern for cardiac ischemia was ruled out by normal EKGs, undetectable troponin levels on two occasions, and a normal exercise stress test. Her symptoms improved with pantoprazole, supporting a diagnosis of dyspepsia. She was found to have elevated blood pressure during admission, prompting an increase in lisinopril from 5mg to 10mg. Her anxiety, exacerbated by significant social stressors including her grandson’s uncertain living situation, was addressed with ongoing therapy and social work support. She remained stable throughout her stay, was discharged home on updated medications, and advised to follow up with her cardiologist and primary care provider.
problems: Dyspepsia and other specified disorders of function of stomach
